tagline: Down the Root River, with buggies for company.
intro: Highway 16 takes its time through the Root River valley, 88 miles from La Crescent to Dexter, under wooded dolomite bluffs and between pasture and fields. Trout streams come down out of the hills to meet it, and on the country roads an Amish buggy is simply part of the traffic.

The valley towns come along one after another, Houston and Rushford and Preston. Between Spring Valley and Preston a state park keeps a village the railroad passed by and a cave that never changes its weather.

moments.title: Lanesboro
moments.text: At Lanesboro, a town of about 700, the South Branch of the Root River spills over a dam across from Sylvan Park.

moments.title: Historic Forestville
moments.text: A trade town that faded after the railroad went elsewhere in 1868, kept in 1899 by costumed interpreters minding the general store and the barn.

moments.title: Mystery Cave
moments.text: Minnesota's longest cave holds at a steady 48 degrees among its stalactites and underground pools, seen on naturalist-led tours.
